descs.t: LISA's new EP Press Play debuted at number one on the Worldwide iTunes Albums Chart and at number one on the European iTunes Albums Chart, while her single Tarantino entered the Global Spotify chart at No. 44 with 1,911,491 streams. We go through every chart Press Play landed on and what the Spotify numbers add.

LISA's Press Play topped the Worldwide iTunes Albums Chart, yet some accounts say four tracks failed to chart on Spotify and her streams are declining. We set the iTunes wins beside the Spotify numbers and ask what this debut really says about LISA's solo career.

LISA is back, and her fans pushed Press Play to number one on iTunes worldwide and past Jennie's Fallen Angel on the European chart. From fans pleading for album sales to a number one YouTube trending music video, we look at the army behind this debut and whether the critics have a point.

intro.plain: LISA's new EP Press Play just debuted at number one on the Worldwide iTunes Albums Chart, and her single Tarantino entered the Global Spotify chart at 44 with 1.91 million streams. Let's walk through where it charted and what it means. Tell me in the chat: is Tarantino the best song on the EP?
intro.mid: Two stories are running about LISA today. Press Play is number one on iTunes worldwide and in Europe. But some accounts say four tracks missed the Spotify charts and her streams are slipping. So which one is true? Both numbers are real, and I'll put them side by side. Chat, be honest: is LISA's solo career rising or levelling off?
intro.bold: LISA is back, and her fans just took over iTunes. Press Play is number one worldwide, it beat Jennie's Fallen Angel on the European chart, and fans literally begged people to buy the album. Then the haters showed up with Spotify numbers. Let's settle it. Chat, drop it now: are you team LISA or team skeptic?

hook.plain: LISA's Press Play just went number one on iTunes worldwide. Here is every chart it landed on, and what the Spotify numbers add.
hook.mid: Number one on iTunes, number 44 on Spotify. LISA's new EP is telling two different stories, and by the end you will know which one counts.
hook.bold: Her fans begged the world to buy it, and it worked. LISA's Press Play is number one worldwide. Now let's see if the haters have a point.

descs.t: Ethan Klein says he is giving up ownership and financial stakes in H3 podcasts and businesses after his wife Hila Klein said he admitted to a 6 month affair. The H3 Podcast crew says it will no longer work with him. We go through what Hila said, what Ethan said and what happens to H3.

Ethan Klein has asked the public to respect his family's privacy, but his critics point out he rarely gave others the same courtesy. With a resurfaced clip going viral and the H3 crew walking away, we look at the fallout and what it means for one of the internet's loudest voices.

Ethan Klein spent years tearing into his critics. Now his wife Hila says he admitted to a 6 month affair, his own crew has walked away and he is begging for privacy. We break down the scandal, the resurfaced clips and why so many people say he had this coming.

intro.plain: Big news from the H3 world. Hila Klein says her husband Ethan admitted to a 6 month affair, and Ethan says he is giving up his ownership and financial stake in H3 and its businesses. The podcast crew says they will no longer work with him. Let's go through it. Chat, does H3 survive without Ethan?
intro.mid: Ethan Klein is asking for privacy after Hila Klein said he admitted to an affair. That is a hard ask from a man known for going after people online. His crew has walked away and he is handing over his stake in H3. Chat, be honest: do you feel any sympathy for Ethan Klein?
intro.bold: Ethan Klein threw it all away. His wife Hila says he admitted to a 6 month affair, his own crew dropped him, and the guy who attacked everyone online now wants privacy. Even Hasan was left speechless at an old clip. Chat, tell me straight: is this karma?

hook.plain: Ethan Klein is giving up his stake in H3 after Hila Klein said he admitted to an affair. Here is what was said, and what comes next.
hook.mid: He made a career out of calling people out. Now Ethan Klein wants privacy. Here is how the H3 scandal unfolded, and why critics are not giving it to him.
hook.bold: A 6 month affair, a crew that walked out and a career in pieces. Ethan Klein lost it all in days, and the old clips show it coming.

descs.t: A shooting in Trappes, in the Paris suburbs, killed one person and wounded others in what officials call a suspected racist attack, and a suspect has been arrested. It came as hundreds of thousands protested across France and troops were sent into Paris. We go through what is known about the attack and the unrest around it.

President Macron called the Trappes shooting the first terrorist act in France aimed at people for their skin colour or religion. Critics answered that Mohammed Merah murdered Jewish children 14 years ago. We look at the attack, Macron's claim and why it landed in the middle of mass protests against him.

One person is dead in Trappes, Paris is full of troops and protesters, and Macron is telling France this is its first racist terror attack. The families of Mohammed Merah's victims would disagree. We condemn the attack, and we look at why every act of terror deserves the same name.

intro.plain: A gunman opened fire in Trappes, in the Paris suburbs, killing one person and wounding others in what officials call a suspected racist attack. A suspect is under arrest. All this while protests fill Paris and troops are on the streets. Let's go through what we know. Chat, what do you think France does next?
intro.mid: Macron says the Trappes shooting is the first terror attack in French history aimed at people for their race or religion. That claim is already under fire, because Mohammed Merah murdered Jewish children 14 years ago. And it comes as over 400,000 people protest against him. Chat, is Macron right or rewriting history?
intro.bold: One person is dead in Trappes, and Macron calls it France's first racist terror attack. First? Mohammed Merah murdered Jewish children 14 years ago. Every act of terror is evil, and the victims all deserve to be remembered. Meanwhile Paris is full of troops and protesters. Chat, tell me: has Macron lost France?

hook.plain: One person is dead after a shooting in Trappes near Paris, and a suspect is under arrest. Here is what we know, and the protests around it.
hook.mid: Macron called it France's first racist terror attack. Within hours, people were naming Mohammed Merah. Here is why that one sentence matters.
hook.bold: A gunman kills one near Paris, and Macron says France has never seen this before. The Jewish children Mohammed Merah murdered say otherwise.

descs.t: The Trump Justice Department has sued Alaska to block certification of its Senate race over a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot, and Mary Peltola's campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee have moved to fight it. Senator Lisa Murkowski has attacked the lawsuit. We go through the ballot, the lawsuit and the legal arguments.

Republicans like Stephen Miller call a second Dan Sullivan on Alaska's ballot a scheme to confuse voters, while Mary Peltola calls the DOJ lawsuit a desperate attempt to silence Alaskans. We look at what the ballot actually shows, what the lawsuit asks a judge to do and who has the stronger case.

Two men named Dan Sullivan are on Alaska's Senate ballot, and only one of them is the senator. The Trump DOJ is suing, Murkowski is furious and Democrats rushed to court overnight. We break down the decoy candidate fight that could swing control of the Senate.

intro.plain: Alaska's Senate race just landed in court. The Trump Justice Department sued to block certification over a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot, and Mary Peltola's campaign and national Democrats moved to fight it. Lisa Murkowski is attacking the lawsuit. Let's go through what is on the ballot and what the case asks. Chat, is a second Dan Sullivan fair game?
intro.mid: Here is the fight. Republicans say Democrats put a second Dan Sullivan on Alaska's ballot to confuse voters. Democrats say the DOJ is trying to block an election before it happens. Murkowski sided against the DOJ. I'll lay out the ballot and the lawsuit side by side. Chat, who has the better case here?
intro.bold: There are two Dan Sullivans on Alaska's Senate ballot, and only one is the senator. Stephen Miller calls it a fraud scheme. The Trump DOJ sued. And Lisa Murkowski is raging at her own party's administration. This could decide the Senate. Chat, decoy or dirty trick, what do you call it?

hook.plain: The Trump DOJ is suing Alaska over its Senate race, and it all comes down to two men named Dan Sullivan. Here is what is on the ballot.
hook.mid: One side calls it a decoy candidate. The other calls the lawsuit an attempt to rig the result. Here is what Alaska's ballot really shows.
hook.bold: Two Dan Sullivans, one Senate seat and a lawsuit filed before a single vote is counted. Alaska just became the strangest race of the year.

descs.t: Ukraine's Starlink and Starshield service is back to the speeds it had before the restrictions, President Zelensky says, and the Defence Ministry reports stable links at more than 400 km/h. We go through what was restricted, how it was restored and why it matters for drones and fast-moving equipment on the frontline.

Elon Musk claims Ukraine violated Starlink terms by using a civilian service for offensive drone strikes, while Zelensky thanked President Trump and the State Department for restoring it. We look at the blame game between Musk and the White House and the gap between Starlink and Starshield.

Ukraine's drones and fast-moving equipment were held back by a speed limit on Starlink. Now the links are back at full power after a public fight between Elon Musk and the White House. We break down how close the frontline came to losing its eyes and who holds the switch.

intro.plain: Ukraine's Starlink and Starshield are back at full speed. Zelensky says operations are restored to where they were before the restrictions, and the Defence Ministry reports stable links at more than 400 km/h. Let's go through what was limited and how it came back. Chat, should a war depend on one company's satellites?
intro.mid: Ukraine's Starlink is restored, but the blame game is not over. Elon Musk says Ukraine broke the rules by using a civilian service for offensive drone strikes. Zelensky thanked Trump and Rubio for fixing it. So who was right? I'll walk you through both sides. Chat, was Musk right to limit it?
intro.bold: Ukraine's drones were hobbled by a single setting on Starlink. Above a certain speed, the link dropped. Now it is back at full power after Elon Musk and the White House fought it out in public. Think about that: one switch. Chat, tell me, who should control that switch?

hook.plain: Ukraine's Starlink is back at full speed. Here is what was restricted, how it was restored and what it means on the frontline.
hook.mid: Musk says Ukraine broke the terms. Zelensky thanked Trump. Somewhere between the two is the truth about who controls Ukraine's battlefield internet.
hook.bold: One speed limit on one satellite network, and Ukraine's drones were in trouble. It is fixed for now. Here is why that should worry everyone.

descs.t: France deployed about 70,000 police officers as protesters marched across its cities for another weekend, and nearly 1,000 people have been arrested, the interior minister says. Over 400,000 people marched according to the Interior Ministry. We go through the clashes in Lyon, the march in Orléans and what police say they prevented.

France is bracing for another weekend of protests with 70,000 police on the streets, while the National Rally reelected Bardella and counter protesters marched against its congress. We look at whether the security push is working and what the arrest numbers say.

France put 70,000 police on the streets to stop more riots, and the first clashes broke out in Lyon anyway. Nearly 1,000 arrests, looting attempts stopped at town halls and police stations, and a country on edge. We break down the weekend France feared and who is behind the chaos.

intro.plain: France is in its second weekend of mass protests. About 70,000 police were deployed, and the interior minister says nearly 1,000 people have been arrested. The first clashes were seen in Lyon. Let's go through what happened city by city. Chat, where are you watching from, and is it calm there?
intro.mid: France put 70,000 police on the streets today and still saw clashes. Over 400,000 marched by the Interior Ministry's count, and nearly 1,000 were arrested. At the same time the National Rally reelected Bardella. So is the state getting control back? Chat, does this crackdown work or make it worse?
intro.bold: France is bracing for mayhem again. 70,000 police, nearly 1,000 arrests and the first clashes already in Lyon. Police say they stopped attacks on town halls and police stations. This is a country fighting for its own streets. Chat, tell me straight: who is to blame for France's chaos?

hook.plain: France deployed 70,000 police for another weekend of protests, and nearly 1,000 people were arrested. Here is where it turned tense.
hook.mid: 70,000 police on the streets, and the clashes started anyway. Here is what this weekend tells us about who controls France right now.
hook.bold: Lyon, Orléans, Paris. France threw 70,000 police at the streets to stop another round of riots. Here is how the night really went.
